answer: Batch Normalization prevents small parameter changes from amplifying into larger changes in activations and gradients, so the training doesn't get stuck in saturated regimes. answer: Greedy action selection always picks the action with the highest estimated value to maximize immediate reward. Epsilon-greedy methods do the same most of the time, but with small probability epsilon they instead select a random action. This lets epsilon-greedy methods explore inferior actions occasionally, whereas greedy methods never do.

answer: The TD error, written as delta sub t, is the difference between the estimated value of the current state and a better estimate formed from the next reward and the next state's value. Specifically, it equals the next reward plus gamma times the value of the next state, minus the value of the current state. The book also describes it as a sort of error measuring the difference between the estimated value of S t and the better estimate R t plus 1 plus gamma times V of S t plus 1.
